'''George Isaac Glauberman''' (born 1941) is a [[mathematician]] at the [[University of Chicago]] who works on [[finite simple group]]s. He proved the [[ZJ theorem]] and the [[Z* theorem|Z<sup>*</sup> theorem]].

Born in [[New York City]] on March 3, 1941, Glauberman did his undergraduate studies at the [[Polytechnic Institute of New York University|Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]], graduating in 1961, and earned a master's degree from [[Harvard University]] in 1962.<ref>[http://www.math.uchicago.edu/~gg/ggcv.html Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2013-07-21.</ref> He obtained his [[PhD]] degree from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1965, under the supervision of [[Richard Bruck]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=6606}}</ref> He has had 22 PhD students, including [[Ahmed Chalabi]] and [[Peter Landrock]].  He has co-authored with [[J.&nbsp;L. Alperin]], [[Simon P. Norton]], [[Zvi Arad]], and Justin Lynd.

In 1970 he was an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] at [[Nice]]. In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref>
